usageExplainer.title: What counts as a game?
usageExplainer.copy: A game is a basketball session in your library, usually tied to one matchup and date. Usage is based on processed video duration, not the number of game records.
usageExplainer.scaleCopy: Footage over 60 minutes simply continues against the same analysis-minute allowance.

pricing.note: Indicative product pricing only. Billing is not active during private beta. Final allowances, feature availability and paid launch terms will be confirmed before charging customers.

intro.title: Know what CourtFlux can do
intro.copy: The product story separates benchmarked capabilities from active development and the longer-term coaching vision, so beta users know what to expect.

betaLab.title: The test environment stays a test environment.
betaLab.copy: Configure clips, tune detector thresholds, run the pipeline and inspect diagnostics without mixing engineering controls into the customer-facing marketing experience.

faq.question: Who is CourtFlux for?
faq.answer: CourtFlux is being built for basketball coaches, teams, academies and performance analysts who want to get more useful information from the game film they already record.

faq.question: What kind of video can CourtFlux analyse?
faq.answer: CourtFlux is being developed around basketball game footage where the court and players are sufficiently visible. Camera position, resolution, occlusion and motion blur can affect analysis quality.

faq.question: Do I need specialist cameras?
faq.answer: No proprietary capture system is required by the product direction. CourtFlux is designed around normal basketball game film.

faq.question: How do analysis minutes work?
faq.answer: Usage is based on processed video duration rather than the number of uploads. A 3-minute clip uses about 3 analysis minutes and a 60-minute recording uses about 60.

faq.question: What counts as a full game?
faq.answer: For pricing guidance, a full game means up to 60 minutes of uploaded video. A game can still be stored as a matchup or session in the product; usage is based on the actual video duration processed.

faq.question: What is available in the beta today?
faq.answer: The current benchmark focuses on player detection and tracking, team classification, ball detection, temporal ball tracking and processing diagnostics. Court mapping, possessions, events and tactical intelligence are being developed in stages.

faq.question: Does AI replace the coach or analyst?
faq.answer: No. CourtFlux is intended to surface evidence and reduce manual video work while keeping basketball judgement with the coach or analyst.
